NOT COVERED:
1. One viewport only. No counts at the 320px reflow floor or below `md`, where the sidebar is replaced by the TopBar disclosure (TopBar.tsx:155-179) and the supplier gains MobileTabBar (SupplierShell.tsx:39) — element counts there are certainly different and were not taken.
2. English only (`?lng=en`). No Arabic/RTL pass, so nothing here says whether the same counts or nesting hold in the mirrored layout.
3. Two personas. officer@mots.local and supplier@mots.local. procurement_manager, evaluator, reviewer, ministry_viewer and system_admin see different sidebar sets (shells/navigation.ts lists 31 back-office destinations; the officer sees 6) and different action sets — the manager-only Finalize step (RfqDetailPage.tsx:1078) was never rendered, only read.
4. Four screens audited out of ~65 routed. The 26 screens in DESIGN-IS-2026-09-10/shots/ and the ~40 routes with no screenshot were not counted; the repeatedPatterns counts that span the whole codebase (26 caption duplicates, 137 label sites, 11 list screens) are grep-derived over source, not verified screen by screen.

Neither primary task was clicked through end to end; the step lists are the controls the source renders for each state, cross-checked against four real tenders in four different states (Draft RFQ-DEMO-0116, Open RFQ-DEMO-0110, Under evaluation RFQ-DEMO-0105, Approved RFQ-DEMO-0118). Whether a step is skippable in practice — e.g. whether a tender can be submitted with zero requirements — was not tested.
6. `Input.invalid`'s visual consequence is source-derived, not photographed. I did not trigger a validation error in the browser and sample the computed border colour.
7. The Owner-column uniformity (25/25 "Demo Procurement Officer") is a fact about this seeded database, not about the product.
8. Counting rule caveat: focusable counts exclude `disabled` controls and anything inside `[aria-hidden="true"]` (which removes Radix's mirror <select>, Select.tsx:33). Raw counts including those are given in interactiveElementCount for comparison. A Select trigger counts as 1; its portal options are not in the DOM until opened and were not counted.
9. Nesting depth is the deepest leaf path, measured by walking the DOM below <main id="main">. It does not report the median depth, and React fragments/context providers are invisible to the DOM walk (the 10-component React chain was read from source instead).

a11y.knownGaps:
Gaps the instruments themselves record, quoted from where they are written down:

1. themeContrast.test.ts:24-26 — the guard checks the pairs the design intends; "A component that puts together a pair nobody intended is out of reach, and that is what the axe sweep over the routes is for. Two instruments, neither sufficient alone."
2. SkipLink.test.tsx:14-17 and SkipLink.tsx:9-12 — axe's skip-link rule is best-practice-tagged and the scans run wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag22aa only; 137 axe checks were green throughout the period the product had no skip link, and "would be green again the day it lost one".
3. app-a11y.spec.ts:137-143 — a previously undetected false-clean: `?lng=ar` was overwritten by the fixture's account language on every authenticated route, so roughly 60 of 68 routes ran both of their scans against the English LTR interface while the file reported 137 scans "in both languages". Found by a design audit, not by any instrument; the dir/lang assertion at lines 142-143 is the fix.
4. app-a11y.spec.ts:8-14 — the file exists because tests/e2e/storybook-axe.spec.ts scanned 8 isolated components and 0 of 18 application routes while believing it covered the app.
5. themeReachability.test.ts:9-25 — tokens.css carries a full dark palette that themeContrast checks in 83 pairs and no user has ever seen, because nothing applies .theme-dark or [data-theme="dark"]; the reason is recorded in UNREACHABLE_BECAUSE (lines 35-41) rather than fixed.
6. app-keyboard.spec.ts:9-17 — coverage is reduced to 3 Radix component types plus one page's focus order on the strength of a source grep; that grep's stated result is now out of date (see unresolvedA11yGaps).
7. playwright.config.ts:59-66 — the config states plainly what axe cannot do: "axe cannot verify tab order, focus traps, or that a control is operable rather than merely focusable", and "axe does not check that an aria-describedby id target exists or holds the visible error text" (the latter is why tests/e2e/app-error-association.spec.ts exists).
8. ACCESSIBILITY.md:115-119 requires that on navigation focus moves to the new page's <h1> or the skip-to-content target and that the page title is announced through a polite live region. I found no instrument asserting either, and no route-change focus management in the shells (AppShell.tsx, TopBar.tsx, Sidebar.tsx carry none).
